Date: 12/8/26

This document puts the cost of a negative-steering run next to the cost of the
structure predictors in `structure-prediction-benchmarking`, on the same 18
Tier-1 HMA decoy and AVR targets and the same cluster hardware.

The comparison is not single-valued. A benchmark run is 5 seeds × 5
diffusion samples = 25 predictions (ESMFold2 emits 5). A negative-steering run
is a cold start plus, if the cold start fails, `negsteer_n_designs` steering
sets × 3 seeds × 5 samples, with a re-prediction for every design whose
mutations needed reverting. Cost per run therefore scales with the number of
steering sets, and cost per prediction does not. The figure reports per-run cost
and the prediction count that explains it, and the paired tests below report
per-prediction cost.

Two steering cohorts are shown, because the parameter that dominates cost was
set differently in each.

* 20 steering sets, the 18-target benchmark under `experiments/benchmarking/`.
  A median of 305 predictions per run.
* 3 steering sets, the 128 designed sequences of the AVR-PikF campaign
  (`crystal_full_test_contig` in `receptor-resurfacing-pipeline`). A median of
  50 predictions per run. This is the setting the pipeline ships with.

They differ in more than the steering-set count, so read the gap between them as
the effect of the configuration as a whole rather than of that one parameter.
The campaign also used a smaller candidate pool (10 against 12), took its
protected set from the design region rather than the true interface, ran with
`negsteer_no_kernels: true`, and ran many sequences concurrently
(`max_boltz2_parallel: 24`), which can inflate wall-clock through contention.
The per-prediction figures are nonetheless close (20.5 s against 22.1 s), so the
per-run gap is close to pure sampling depth.

MSA search is counted. Benchmark wall-clock is `standalone_elapsed_s`, which
folds in the shared ColabFold MSA search for the models that depend on it
(Boltz-1 and Boltz-2 with an MSA, and ColabFold). Using the raw `elapsed_s`
would hand those three a free MSA and understate them by roughly 35 min each.
This is the same convention as that repo's own compute-cost analysis.

Wall-clock for steering is every stage of the run summed (plan, predict-one,
collect, reversion, harvest, finalize, aggregate, metrics), not just the GPU
time. Both cohorts ran on the `jic-gpu` queue with `--gres=gpu:1`, so they are
comparable.

Regenerate the input CSV with:

```bash
python3 analysis/03-compute-cost/stage_runtime_comparison.py
```

## 1. Setup

```{python}
import math
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

HERE = Path.cwd()
if not (HERE / "runtime_comparison.csv").exists():
    HERE = Path("analysis/03-compute-cost")

rt = pd.read_csv(HERE / "runtime_comparison.csv")

NEGSTEER_20 = "Boltz-2 + negative steering (steering sets = 20)"
NEGSTEER_3 = "Boltz-2 + negative steering (steering sets = 3)"
# The variant is shown by colour, so the y axis carries the bare model name and the
# same model can appear more than once.
VARIANT_COLOR = {
    "no_msa": "#4C72B0",
    "msa": "#C44E52",
    "restraints": "#8172B2",
    "negsteer": "#55A868",
}
VARIANT_LABEL = {
    "no_msa": "No MSA",
    "msa": "MSA",
    "restraints": "restraints from the reference",
    "negsteer": "negative steering",
}

TIME_TICKS = [1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200]        # minutes
PER_PRED_TICKS = [2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500]  # seconds

FIGDIR = HERE / "thesis-figures"
FIGDIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


def save_fig(fig, name):
    fig.savefig(FIGDIR / f"{name}.png", dpi=200, bbox_inches="tight", pad_inches=0.05)


def readable_log(axis, ticks):
    axis.set_ticks(ticks)
    axis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:g}"))
    axis.set_minor_locator(plt.NullLocator())
```

## 2. Cost per run

One point per model and variant, the median across the targets that model ran.
Spread is small relative to the differences between models (the tightest combos
vary by seconds, the widest by tens of minutes), and showing it obscured the
comparison, so it is reported in the table rather than drawn.

```{python}
med = (rt.groupby(["model", "variant"])
         .agg(elapsed_min=("elapsed_min", "median"),
              sec_per_prediction=("sec_per_prediction", "median"),
              n_predictions=("n_predictions", "median"),
              n=("target", "size"))
         .reset_index()
         .sort_values("elapsed_min")
         .reset_index(drop=True))

ys = np.arange(len(med))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.0, 5.2))

ax.scatter(med["elapsed_min"], ys, s=78,
           color=[VARIANT_COLOR[a] for a in med["variant"]],
           edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.7, zorder=3)

# The two steering rows are far longer than any model name, so they wrap rather
# than push the plotting area off the page.
ax.set_yticks(ys)
ax.set_yticklabels([m.replace(" (steering", "\n(steering") for m in med["model"]],
                   fontsize=10)
ax.set_ylim(-0.8, len(med) - 0.4)
ax.invert_yaxis()   # fastest at the top
ax.set_xscale("log")
readable_log(ax.xaxis, TIME_TICKS)
ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=9.5)
ax.set_xlabel("Median wall-clock per run (minutes, log scale)", fontsize=10)
ax.grid(axis="x", ls=":", color="#CCCCCC", lw=0.6, zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)

# Predictions per run, as a right-hand column. Without it the ranking invites
# the wrong reading, since steering's run buys an order of magnitude more
# predictions than any benchmark run does.
trans = ax.get_yaxis_transform()
for y, n in zip(ys, med["n_predictions"]):
    ax.text(1.05, y, f"{int(n)}", transform=trans, ha="left", va="center",
            fontsize=9.5, clip_on=False)
ax.text(1.05, -0.85, "predictions\nper run", transform=trans, ha="left",
        va="center", fontsize=9.5, style="italic", clip_on=False)

handles = [plt.Line2D([], [], ls="none", marker="o", markersize=8,
                      mfc=VARIANT_COLOR[a], mec="black", mew=0.7)
           for a in ["no_msa", "msa", "restraints", "negsteer"]]
ax.legend(handles, [VARIANT_LABEL[a] for a in ["no_msa", "msa", "restraints", "negsteer"]],
          loc="lower center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.01), ncol=2, frameon=False,
          fontsize=9.5, borderaxespad=0.0)
save_fig(fig, "compute_cost_comparison")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
spread = (rt.groupby(["model", "variant"])
            .agg(n=("target", "size"),
                 predictions=("n_predictions", "median"),
                 median_min=("elapsed_min", "median"),
                 min_min=("elapsed_min", "min"),
                 max_min=("elapsed_min", "max"),
                 median_s_per_pred=("sec_per_prediction", "median"),
                 median_peak_rss_gb=("peak_rss_gb", "median"))
            .round(1).sort_values("median_min").reset_index())
spread
```

- At 20 steering sets, negative steering is the most expensive method here, at a
  median of 111 min against 109 min for AlphaFold2-Multimer and 40 to 43 min for
  Boltz-1, Boltz-2 and ColabFold once their MSA search is counted.
- At 3 steering sets it is cheaper per run than every MSA-based combination, at
  17.2 min against 22.8 min for AlphaFold3 with an MSA. Per run the claim depends
  entirely on the steering-set count, and it holds at the shipped setting.
- The difference between the two cohorts is sampling depth rather than
  per-prediction overhead. 305 predictions per run against 50, at 22.1 s and
  20.5 s per prediction.
- The overhead of steering itself is modest. Steering runs at 22.1 s per
  prediction against unsteered Boltz-2's 12.4 s, so planning, contact analysis,
  reversion and final metrics add about 75% on top of the raw Boltz-2 call.
- Some units never steer. Three of the 18 benchmark targets and 22 of the 128
  campaign sequences had a cold start that passed on every seed, so the run
  exited after 15 predictions. Cost is conditional on the cold start failing.

## 3. Cost against memory

The thesis figure. Wall-clock and peak memory on the same axes, so the two
resources that actually bound throughput can be read together, with negative
steering placed among the predictors rather than in a separate figure.

Memory comes from different tooling per cohort (see
`stage_runtime_comparison.py`), and the two measurements agree closely where
they overlap, so the axis is comparable across every point. It is host RAM, not
VRAM, which is usually the real constraint.

Reference-restrained points share the No MSA colour, as they are a no-MSA variant,
and carry `(constr)` in their label. The two steering points carry a bare
steering-set count, which the legend spells out, because that count is what
separates them.

```{python}
SCATTER_COLOR = {"no_msa": VARIANT_COLOR["no_msa"], "restraints": VARIANT_COLOR["no_msa"],
                 "msa": VARIANT_COLOR["msa"], "negsteer": VARIANT_COLOR["negsteer"]}
SCATTER_LEGEND = [("no_msa", "No MSA"), ("msa", "MSA"),
                  ("negsteer", "Negative steering\n(steering sets)")]

med2 = (rt.groupby(["model", "variant"])
          .agg(runtime=("elapsed_min", "median"),
               memory=("peak_rss_gb", "median"))
          .reset_index())


def scatter_label(model, variant):
    if variant == "negsteer":
        # Bare count; the legend says these are steering sets.
        return "Boltz-2 (%s)" % model.split("= ")[1].rstrip(")")
    return f"{model} (constr)" if variant == "restraints" else model


med2["label"] = [scatter_label(m, a) for m, a in zip(med2["model"], med2["variant"])]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.4, 6.4))
for variant in ["msa", "restraints", "no_msa", "negsteer"]:
    sub = med2[med2["variant"] == variant]
    ax.scatter(sub["runtime"], sub["memory"], s=90, color=SCATTER_COLOR[variant],
               alpha=0.65, edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.6,
               zorder=5 if variant == "negsteer" else 4)

# Nudged so the near-coincident pairs (each Boltz model against its restrained
# variant, and 20-set steering against AlphaFold2-Multimer) stay readable.
LABEL_LEFT = {("ESMFold2", "no_msa"), ("Boltz-2", "no_msa"),
              ("Boltz-1", "no_msa"), ("ColabFold", "no_msa"),
              ("AlphaFold2-Multimer", "msa")}
LABEL_BELOW = {("Boltz-2", "restraints"), ("Boltz-1", "restraints")}
for _, r in med2.iterrows():
    key = (r["model"], r["variant"])
    if key in LABEL_BELOW:
        dx, dy, ha, va = 0, -11, "center", "top"
    elif key in LABEL_LEFT:
        dx, dy, ha, va = -8, 0, "right", "center"
    else:
        dx, dy, ha, va = 8, 0, "left", "center"
    ax.annotate(r["label"], (r["runtime"], r["memory"]), fontsize=7.5,
                xytext=(dx, dy), textcoords="offset points", ha=ha, va=va,
                zorder=6)

ax.set_xscale("log")
readable_log(ax.xaxis, TIME_TICKS)
ax.set_xlabel("Median wall-clock per run (minutes, log scale)")
ax.set_ylabel("Median peak resident memory (GB)")
ax.set_xlim(right=260)   # room for the right-hand labels at ~110 min
handles = [plt.Line2D([], [], ls="none", marker="o", markersize=8,
                      mfc=SCATTER_COLOR[a], mec="black", mew=0.7, alpha=0.65)
           for a, _ in SCATTER_LEGEND]
ax.legend(handles, [lab for _, lab in SCATTER_LEGEND], loc="center left",
          bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 0.5), frameon=True, fontsize=10)
save_fig(fig, "compute_cost_tradeoff")
plt.show()
```

- Negative steering costs no more memory than the Boltz-2 it wraps, 4.6 to 5.1
  GB against 5.0 GB unsteered. Memory is set by the prediction model, so the
  engine's extra stages are not what bounds how many can run at once.
- The two steering points sit an order of magnitude apart in wall-clock and on
  top of each other in memory, which is the sampling-depth difference of the
  previous section seen on a second axis.
- At 20 steering sets it lands next to AlphaFold2-Multimer in wall-clock while
  using roughly a fifth of the memory, so under a memory cap it parallelises far
  better than that comparison alone suggests.

## 4. Is the per-prediction cost of steering below the MSA models?

Paired within target, since targets differ in size and the same targets are run
by every method. The paired quantity is the ratio of negative steering's
per-prediction cost to the other method's, so a ratio below 1 means steering is
cheaper per prediction. Reported as the median ratio with a bootstrap 95%
interval, plus an exact two-sided sign test on the paired differences.

```{python}
def sign_test(diffs):
    """Exact two-sided sign test p-value. Ties dropped."""
    d = np.asarray([x for x in diffs if x != 0])
    n, k = len(d), int((np.asarray(d) > 0).sum())
    if n == 0:
        return float("nan")
    tail = sum(math.comb(n, i) for i in range(min(k, n - k) + 1))
    return min(1.0, 2 * tail / 2 ** n)


def boot_median_ci(x, n_boot=10000, seed=0):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    x = np.asarray(x, float)
    draws = np.median(rng.choice(x, size=(n_boot, len(x)), replace=True), axis=1)
    return np.percentile(draws, [2.5, 97.5])


# Paired on target, so this uses the 20-set benchmark cohort. The 3-set campaign
# runs 128 designed sequences against one effector rather than the 18 solved
# complexes, so it shares no targets with the benchmark and cannot be paired
# against it. It appears in the figure and the table above, not here.
ns = rt[rt["model"] == NEGSTEER_20].set_index("target")["sec_per_prediction"]
rows = []
for _, r in med.iterrows():
    if r["variant"] == "negsteer":
        continue
    other = rt[(rt["model"] == r["model"]) & (rt["variant"] == r["variant"])] \
        .set_index("target")["sec_per_prediction"]
    shared = ns.index.intersection(other.index)
    ratio = (ns[shared] / other[shared]).values
    lo, hi = boot_median_ci(ratio)
    p = sign_test((ns[shared] - other[shared]).values)
    rows.append({
        "vs": f"{r['model']} ({VARIANT_LABEL[r['variant']]})",
        "n paired": len(shared),
        "median ratio": round(float(np.median(ratio)), 2),
        "95% CI": f"{lo:.2f}–{hi:.2f}",
        "p (sign test)": "<0.0001" if p < 1e-4 else f"{p:.4f}",
        "verdict": ("steering cheaper" if hi < 1 else
                    "steering costlier" if lo > 1 else "indistinguishable"),
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

- Steering is cheaper per prediction than every MSA-based combination, and the
  intervals are well clear of 1 in each case. Against AlphaFold2-Multimer the
  ratio is 0.08, against ColabFold, Boltz-1 and Boltz-2 with an MSA it is
  0.21–0.24, and against AlphaFold3 with an MSA it is 0.41.
- Among the no-MSA models it is cheaper only than ESMFold2 (0.38). It is 1.2 to
  5.2 times more expensive per prediction than the other no-MSA combos, which is
  the expected price of the extra Boltz-2 calls and the engine's own stages.
- So the claim holds per prediction at either steering-set count, and it holds
  per run as well at the 3 sets the pipeline ships with. It fails per run only
  at the benchmark's 20 sets, where steering deliberately samples an order of
  magnitude deeper than any single prediction does.

Wall-clock is execution time rather than time-to-result, so queueing is
excluded. One benchmark target has no usable trace row, so the benchmark combos
cover 17 of 18 targets against steering's 18. Both cohorts ran on the same queue
and GPU allocation, but not necessarily on identical nodes. The steering cost is
dominated by a fixed sampling budget (20 designs × 3 seeds) that was not tuned,
so it is a cost of this configuration rather than a floor for the method.
